extracted.intended_audience: general news readers; journalists and editors interested in media ethics
extracted.subtask_description: A short news article reporting on a journalistic fabrication scandal (Stephen Glass) and the magazine's internal investigation, findings, and responses. Focuses on ethics, fact-checking failures, and editorial accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fabricated material in articles
rubrics_metrics.description: A month-long internal inquiry by The New Republic has found that 27 of the 41 articles Stephen Glass wrote ... contained at least partly made up material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit standard: published articles must not include made-up material; the reporting cites examples where a majority of an author's output contained invented content. Example severity note: 'Six articles, three of which the journal has acknowledged as fake, "could be considered entirely or nearly entirely made up."'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid blending fact and fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Many other articles by the 25-year-old journalist were 'a blend of fact and fiction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/expectation: reporting should not mix invented details with factual reporting; blending undermines trust and requires retraction/apology when discovered. The magazine states: 'We offer no excuses for any of this. Only our deepest apologies to all concerned.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not deceive fact-checkers or editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Lane has said Glass 'deliberately deceived' the magazine's fact-checkers with forged notes, fabricated documents, fake press releases as well as a bogus Web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-patterns to avoid: submitting forged notes, fabricated documents, fake press releases, or creating bogus supporting websites to mislead verification processes. Fact-checking procedures must be able to detect and guard against such deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroborate anonymous or off-the-record sources
rubrics_metrics.description: In other cases, Lane said, Glass told fact-checkers that 'certain sources he had were so deep and so dark that they'd asked not to be called back.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation: claims based on anonymous or 'deep and dark' sources require corroboration or clear documentation; treating unverifiable anonymous claims as substitutes for evidence is a red flag for fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify direct quotes, especially in profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: George magazine has said Glass used two fabricated quotes in a profile of Vernon Jordan, one of President Clinton's closest friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific verification practice: confirm quoted material with independent sources or recordings; profiling of public figures requires extra diligence to ensure quotes are genuine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct thorough internal inquiries and publicly account for findings
rubrics_metrics.description: 'From our point of view, we have completed our investigation,' Lane said. 'We feel we know everything that's important to know. We feel that we've presented our fullest accounting to the public.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial standard after misconduct: perform a comprehensive investigation, disclose findings publicly, and present a full accounting to restore transparency and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take prompt disciplinary action and seek cooperation from the author
rubrics_metrics.description: Glass was fired last month as an associate editor after confessing he had 'embellished' a story ... Glass did not contest the findings and apologized ... 'He's cooperating with The New Republic and any other publisher who asks,' Zweifach said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response guidance: when fabrication is confirmed, appropriate disciplinary measures (e.g., termination), demands for cooperation, and public apologies are expected as part of remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and address damage to publication credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: 'I don't believe lasting damage has been done to the credibility of the magazine although certainly this is not the kind of episode we'd like,' he said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial responsibility: evaluate reputational impact, communicate with readers about corrective steps, and implement measures to prevent recurrence to protect long-term credibility.
